investigations.name: biofilm_settling_metabolism
investigations.title: Biofilm settling + metabolism
investigations.objective: When rigid-body cells settle under gravity while feeding, does growth become spatially structured by depth?
investigations.claim: Rigid-body cells settle and pack under gravity while feeding on the nutrient field, and the population grows — a physics-coupled settling biofilm. Whether per-cell growth is structured by depth is suggestive but NOT established at this scale (the mass-vs-depth correlation is weak, ~0.4, not significant at ~10 cells, and varies run to run).

investigations.name: br_particles_dfba
investigations.objective: Particle-embedded metabolism: Brownian agents carry internal dFBA; uptake/secretion couples to fields and biomass accumulates into particle mass/size.
investigations.claim: Brownian agents running internal dFBA accumulate biomass (total particle mass grows) and divide as they feed on the field gradient.

investigations.name: br_particles_kinetics
investigations.objective: Particle–field coupling (kinetics): Brownian agents sample local lattice concentrations and apply Monod-style exchange, modifying both particle mass and fields.
investigations.claim: Brownian agents taking up substrate by Monod kinetics grow in total mass and divide across the lattice.

investigations.name: brownian_particles
investigations.objective: Particle-only baseline: Brownian motion of agents with mass in continuous space (no fields, no metabolism). Checks integrator + particle state schema.
investigations.claim: Mass-carrying agents undergo diffusive Brownian motion — mean-squared displacement grows linearly in time — while the population seeds in.

investigations.name: comets_br_particles_dfba
investigations.objective: Full COMETS-style spatial composite: lattice dFBA + advection–diffusion + Brownian particles with internal dFBA + division. End-to-end coupled scenario.
investigations.claim: The full COMETS composite couples lattice dFBA fields to internal-dFBA agents: field biomass and total agent mass both grow as the population divides.

investigations.name: comets_br_particles_kinetics
investigations.objective: Three-way coupling: spatial dFBA fields + Brownian particle agents that run Monod kinetics locally + diffusion. End-to-end smoke test of the COMETS-style composite stack with kinetic agents.
investigations.claim: COMETS lattice fields feed Monod-kinetic agents whose total mass grows alongside field biomass.

investigations.name: comets_diffusion
investigations.objective: Two-phase coupling (no particles): spatial dFBA on a lattice with advection–diffusion of substrates + biomass. The classic COMETS field-only scenario.
investigations.claim: COMETS-style per-site dFBA on a diffusing lattice grows total biomass while depleting glucose across the field.

investigations.name: comets_nt_particles_dfba
investigations.objective: Mechanochemical + metabolic coupling: Pymunk particles move/collide while COMETS fields diffuse; particles run metabolism (via exchange) against local concentrations.
investigations.claim: Rigid-body dFBA agents settle among COMETS fields while field biomass and total agent mass grow.

investigations.name: community_dfba
investigations.objective: Multi-agent well-mixed community: several independent dFBA instances share the same extracellular pools, creating competition / cross-feeding dynamics without space.
investigations.claim: In a shared-substrate community, glucose is depleted while the E. coli-core population grows — the setting for competition and cross-feeding.

investigations.name: dfba_kinetics_community
investigations.objective: Hybrid community (well-mixed): mixes Monod-kinetic agents with dFBA agents in a shared environment. Demonstrates heterogeneous process composition under one schema.
investigations.claim: A dFBA population and a Monod-kinetic population coexist on a shared glucose pool; both biomasses grow as glucose is consumed.

investigations.name: diffusion_process
investigations.objective: Field transport primitive: finite-volume diffusion/advection on a 2D lattice. Use to validate boundary conditions, stability, and transport timescales.
investigations.claim: Finite-volume transport conserves total field mass (closed boundaries) while redistributing the seeded biomass band.

investigations.name: ecoli_core_dfba
investigations.objective: Single-cell metabolism baseline: dynamic FBA for E. coli core with external glucose/acetate and biomass over time (no space, no particles).
investigations.claim: Dynamic-FBA growth of E. coli core depletes extracellular glucose monotonically as biomass accumulates to a reproducible yield.

investigations.name: ecoli_dfba
investigations.objective: Single-cell metabolism (large model): dynamic FBA using iAF1260 with tracked extracellular fields (glucose/formate) and biomass. Stress-tests solver + exchange wiring.
investigations.claim: Genome-scale (iAF1260) E. coli dFBA converts glucose to biomass, depleting glucose as biomass rises.

investigations.name: monod_kinetics
investigations.objective: Field-only baseline: Monod uptake/growth on a well-mixed substrate pool (no spatial lattice, no particles). Use to sanity-check kinetics + mass balance.
investigations.claim: Monod uptake kinetics drive biomass growth and near-complete glucose depletion in a well-mixed pool.

investigations.name: newtonian_particles
investigations.objective: Physics-only baseline (Pymunk): rigid-body particles with collisions/crowding in continuous space. Use to validate contact dynamics + boundary enforcement.
investigations.claim: Rigid-body agents accumulate under gravity-driven seeding — the mechanics-only baseline.

investigations.name: nutrient_starvation_control
investigations.title: Nutrient-starvation negative control
investigations.objective: With no carbon source, does the dynamic-FBA model correctly fail to grow — the falsification control that the growth signal is real, not an artifact?
investigations.claim: With zero glucose the dynamic-FBA cell does not grow: biomass stays flat within noise. The growth seen in every other study is therefore carbon-driven, not a numerical artifact — this negative control passes by rejecting growth.

investigations.name: reference_demo_x2y2
investigations.objective: Different resolution for the spatio-flux reference demo
investigations.claim: On a fine lattice, the reference model's field biomass and total agent mass grow as two-strain agents feed and divide.

investigations.name: spatial_cross_feeding_bridge
investigations.title: Spatial cross-feeding bridge
investigations.objective: Does a spatially-separated consumer (strain B) grow only where a producer (strain A) secretes a diffusing metabolite?
investigations.claim: Strain A grows on glucose and secretes acetate that diffuses to strain B on the no-glucose side, producing a small, acetate-dependent growth increment in B that does not occur when A is absent — an emergent, spatially-localized cross-feeding dependency (the effect is modest: B grows ~1.6% over the run).

investigations.name: spatial_dfba_process
investigations.objective: Spatial microenvironment (vectorized dFBA): one spatial dFBA process updates all lattice sites as a single structured state. Demonstrates batched execution + field coupling.
investigations.claim: A vectorized spatial dFBA grows total biomass across a glucose gradient as glucose is depleted.

investigations.name: spatial_many_dfba
investigations.objective: Spatial microenvironment (sitewise dFBA): a lattice where each site runs its own dFBA instance. Useful for validating lattice indexing + per-site state isolation.
investigations.claim: Per-site dFBA across the lattice grows total biomass as local glucose is consumed.

investigations.name: spatioflux_reference_demo
investigations.objective: SpatioFlux demonstration reference composite: Newtonian motile particles + particle–field exchange + internal multi-dFBA + Monod/diffusion fields + mass-aggregated division.
investigations.claim: The flagship reference model grows field biomass and total agent mass as two-strain internal-dFBA agents feed and divide.

investigations.name: yeast_dfba
investigations.objective: Single-cell metabolism (yeast): dynamic FBA using iMM904 with extracellular glucose and biomass. Cross-model check of the dFBA pipeline.
investigations.claim: Genome-scale (iMM904) yeast dFBA grows on glucose, depleting it as biomass accumulates.
